summary: multipass is a password manager that keeps every entry in one encrypted text file, the store. An entry has a name, a secret, and a few optional fields such as username and otp. The name is only a label, so nothing in multipass knows which website an entry belongs to, and no program can ask it which entries fit the page it is showing.

This pull request adds one plan, docs/projects/websites/readme.md, at status: ready. It changes no code. The plan gives each entry a repeatable website field and adds multipass find <url>, which prints the names of the entries whose websites match a page. A later browser extension, and the Mac and iPhone app in the passkeys plan, would use that answer to offer the right login on the right site.

• Matching. A stored website matches a page on the same host or a subdomain of it, with the same port, with a leading www. ignored, and never from a stored https address to an http page. This needs no Public Suffix List, the large, often-updated list of domain suffixes that whole-site matching would require.
  • Hints. When nothing matches, find names entries that share only the page's root domain on stderr, with the command that would add the page, and never treats them as matches.
  • Store format. The field needs a new multipass <n> header. The plan takes format 4 and leaves renumbering the passkeys draft, which also claims 4, to the change that builds websites.
  • Deferred. The browser extension and per-site password rules get plans of their own later.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Store format. The number in the store's first line, multipass <n>. The repository changes the store text only by bumping it, so an older multipass refuses a store it cannot read.
  • Root domain. The plan's short rule for a site's registered name: the last two labels of a host, or three after a country code's co, com, and similar.
  • Mergeable store. The store-merge plan: each entry records when it changed, and copies from two Macs merge entry by entry, the newer version winning.
  • Userinfo. The name:password@ part a URL may carry before its host.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
One review at this head asked for changes, with three open findings, shown below at their lines:

  • The plan never says where a URL's host ends, so https://bank.example@evil.example could match the bank's entry.
  • Removing www. before the subdomain test lets a stored www. host match every subdomain of the bare host.
  • The format list that AGENTS.md will point to keeps naming format 4 as the passkey field.

The review also lists eight suggestions that do not block.

groups.title: The websites plan
groups.kicker: A repeatable website field, the matching rule, and the format it needs
intro: The plan is the whole change. Read it in section order: § 2.1 defines the field and how a value is normalized, § 2.2 the matching rule and the root-domain hints, § 2.3 the commands, § 2.4 the store format number, and § 2.5 the files the change that builds it will touch.

Hold two things in mind while reading. First, the matching rule is the plan's security boundary: whatever website::matches accepts is a page where a later extension offers your password, so read each rule in § 2.1 and § 2.2 for a look-alike or attacker-controlled page that it lets through. Second, the plan builds on the mergeable store, which is not on main yet: the example in § 2.1 shows its modified line, and § 2.3 stamps each change through its Store::stamp.

checks.text: The plan's one open question, how strictly a website matches, is recorded as decided by the owner. The browser extension and per-site password rules are explicitly deferred, so no open question blocks status: ready.

files.note: The new plan: the website field, find, the matching and hint rules, and the store format it takes.

checks.text: § 2.1 never says how the host is found in a URL. A parser that reads up to the first : or / takes https://bank.example@evil.example/ as host bank.example, so the bank's entry matches a page on evil.example. The same gap lets a password in userinfo be stored and printed in errors. The review asks for refusing userinfo and backslashes and saying where the host and port end.

Step 1 removes www. before step 4's subdomain test, so a stored https://www.host.example/login matches https://anyone.host.example/, a page another user can control on a platform that gives each user a subdomain. The review asks for ignoring www. only in the equality test.

The store-merge plan's § 2.1 table lists format 4 as the passkey field, and the open mergeable-store pull request marks that plan completed and has AGENTS.md point to the table. This row only names the new number, so the pointer would lead to a record that says format 4 is the passkey field. The review asks for the note itself to say what format 4 adds.
